extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers of projective/conic geometry (advanced undergraduate/graduate level)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, algebraic formulas, and geometric criteria for constructing corresponding points/lines, determining the collinear axis and centre, and for regarding conic sections as collinear/collinearly-situated; plus related classical transversal and hyperboloid propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of corresponding point P' from a given point P
rubrics_metrics.description: Let AB and CD be produced and meet in E, and A'B', C'D' in E'. Through P draw the lines EPR and FPQ meeting AE in Q and AF in R. In the lines AE' and AF' find the points Q' and R' which correspond to Q and R; draw F'Q' and E'R' intersecting in P'; then P' will be the point in one system corresponding to the given point P in the other system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a constructive procedure: find intersections of corresponding sides (E,E'; F,F'), draw through P the two lines determined by those intersections to meet corresponding sides in Q,R, map Q,R to Q',R' on the corresponding sides, then intersect the lines joining to obtain P'. The author remarks a formal proof is unnecessary since the definition of collinear systems ensures the condition is complied with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate (algebraic) transformation for corresponding points
rubrics_metrics.description: If xy are the coordinates of a point in one system, the coordinates of its corresponding point in the other system are given by fractional-linear forms (as obtained from the analytic development): x' = (m' y + n' x + p')/(m y + n x + l), y' = (m'' y + n'' x + p'')/(m y + n x + l) (forms as given in the text, cf. (iii, 3) and the equations derived from (5,6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms are obtained from the equations of lines EPR and FPQ and their images (5,6), and the explicit fractional ratios follow after algebraic elimination; special cases reduce to simpler forms. The denominator my+nx+1 (or similar) is the common factor giving the projective character of the map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric determination of the collinear axis and collinear centre
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce AB and A'B' and let them intersect in the point P; produce AD and A'D' and let them intersect in Q; draw the line PQ, then PQ is the collinear axis. Draw the lines AA', BB' through corresponding points A,A' and B,B', and let them meet in O; then O is the collinear centre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequent facts: each pair of corresponding sides of the collinear quadrilaterals will, when produced, intersect on the collinear axis; the lines through each pair of corresponding points pass through O, the collinear centre. These geometric constructions are offered as methods to locate the axis and centre without analytical computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collinear theory to prove transversal theorem (concurrency of three intersections)
rubrics_metrics.description: If straight lines be drawn from the angles of a triangle through any point in the plane to meet the sides, and the lines joining these points of intersection and the sides of the triangle be produced to meet, the three points of intersection will be in the same straight line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: regard the given interior point as the collinear centre and the points obtained on sides as corresponding points; corresponding sides intersect in the collinear axis, so the three intersection points lie on the same straight line (the collinear axis). The text uses this as an example of applying collineation to classical transversal results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transversal theorem (concurrence of diagonals from three points on a line)
rubrics_metrics.description: From each of three points in the same straight line draw two straight lines so as to form, by their mutual intersections, three quadrilaterals; the diagonals of these quadrilaterals, three and three, (viz. one diagonal of each quadrilateral), will pass through the same point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument treats pairs of corresponding points and lines across the constructed systems and shows the corresponding diagonals intersect in the collinear axis; by symmetry and repetition one obtains concurrency of the indicated diagonals at a point on the axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transversal theorem (fixed point of intersection through constructed lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three points are situated in a straight line, and lines are drawn from these points to any arbitrary point; from two of the given points draw lines to any point in the line passing through the arbitrary point and the third given point, intersecting the two lines drawn through the arbitrary point and the two specified points; then the line drawn through the two points of intersection will always pass through a fixed point in the straight line in which the three given points are situated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: regard the appropriate pairs of points as corresponding and identify their collinear centre O; show that any such constructed pair of intersection points determines a line through O. This is another demonstration of how collineation identifies invariant points/lines for transversal configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pairs of intersections on a conic as corresponding points; chord of contact as collinear axis
rubrics_metrics.description: If straight lines be drawn through a fixed point (taken as origin) intersecting a conic (a line of the second degree), each straight line cuts the curve in two points; each pair of intersections can be regarded as corresponding points of two collinear systems, and the fixed point as the collinear centre. In particular, if from any point P two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a conic, the chord of contact AB may be considered as the collinear axis and the point F as the collinear centre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytically, substituting the projective transform values for coordinates into the conic's equation yields the partner conic; the collinear axis equation reduces to the polar of the origin (equation (4) in the text), and the counter axis is parallel and bisects distances as noted. The chord of contact interpretation gives a geometric method for tangent construction from a point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic criterion: tangents at corresponding points are corresponding lines intersecting on the collinear axis
rubrics_metrics.description: Given corresponding points C and C' on a conic, the equations of the tangents at C and C' are such that, after substituting the projective correspondence, one tangent equation flows into the other; hence these tangents are corresponding lines and intersect in the collinear axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text presents tangent equations (6) and (7) and shows via substitution of the correspondence formulas that they become identical up to the transformation, establishing that tangents at corresponding points meet on the collinear axis (thus supporting the chord-of-contact statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for two conics to be collinear and collinearly situated
rubrics_metrics.description: Two given conics can be regarded as collinear figures if, upon writing for the coordinates in the equation of one conic the fractional-linear expressions giving correspondence, the resulting equation can be made identical with the second conic. This gives five equations of condition in the parameters of the transformation, leaving three parameters free (so three may be arbitrarily chosen provided no imaginary expressions arise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text works a detailed example: two conics touched by two given straight lines inclined at a given angle, with the intersection of the tangents taken as the collinear centre. It derives explicit conditional equations (numbered in the text) and shows how signs/values (e.g., of quantities h and h') determine whether parameter values are real or imaginary and thus the relative positional cases of the curves (both on same side of origin, on opposite sides, etc.). The collinear axes in the double-valued parameter case lead to two axes whose sum/difference give the polars (chords of contact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersections of two collinear conics and collinear axes
rubrics_metrics.description: The collinear axes of two collinearly-situated conics pass through the intersections of both curves; conversely, shared properties such as confocality imply the common focus is a collinear centre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic elimination and combination of the two conic equations (using the transformation parameters and multipliers h,K etc.) shows the intersection points satisfy the product of the collinear axis equations; thus the axes pass through curve intersections. The special case of confocal conics is noted: their common focus acts as collinear centre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of a parallelepiped from three skew lines (Modern Geometry proposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon any three lines in space, two of which are in the same plane, nor all three parallel to the same plane, a parallelepiped may be constituted having these lines as three non-contiguous and non-parallel edges; and there can be only one such parallelepiped constituted on the same three lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: through each given line draw the unique plane parallel to one of the other two lines; these three pairs of parallel planes intersect to form the parallelepiped. Consequent properties: the diagonals AA', BB', CC', DD' meet in a single point P and bisect each other; certain edges form a twisted hexagon whose opposite sides are equal and parallel; traces of these edges on any cutting plane lie on a conic section (proof via parallelism and use of transversal ratios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry and conic-section trace properties of hyperboloid generatrices / twisted hexagon
rubrics_metrics.description: Generatrices and corresponding symmetrical generatrices form a unique system on the hyperboloid; cutting any plane through the twisted hexagon's six edges yields six intersection points that lie on a conic. For each generatrix of the first mode there is a parallel symmetric generatrix of the second mode, and the surface is symmetric about the center P of the parallelepiped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text details how traces of generatrices and directrices on a cutting plane form two triangles with corresponding parallel sides; by using transversal ratio identities and known theorems (converse of Pascal, copolar triangles), the six intersection points are shown to lie on a conic. Additional remarks show similarity/symmetric placement of these conics under variation of the parallelopiped.
